title: 个人理财 · Day 12 · 保险第一原则
title_en: Personal Finance · Day 12 · First Principles of Insurance

questions.question: 既然每份保险按期望值算都是亏的，一个理性的人为什么还应该买某些保险？
options: 因为保险公司在长期会把保费的一部分作为投资收益返还给投保人
因为只要选对了保险产品、算准了条款，期望赔付就能超过所交的保费
它用可预算的小支出削掉会让计划报废的尾部损失
因为身体好、开车稳的人出险概率低，买保险的实际成本更低
questions.explanation: 保费必然大于期望赔付，买的从来不是收益，而是削掉损失分布的尾巴；财富增长看连乘，一次归零就出局，所以挡住「出局」的负期望溢价也是理性的。认为「身体好就少买」是文中点名的误区：要保的恰恰是那个「不像你」的低概率情形。
questions.question_en: If every insurance policy loses money in expected-value terms, why should a rational person still buy some insurance?
options_en: Over the long run, insurers return part of premiums to policyholders as investment returns
With the right product and carefully worked-out terms, expected payouts can exceed premiums
It swaps a small, predictable cost for removing tail losses that would wreck the plan
Healthy people and careful drivers are unlikely to claim, so their real cost of insurance is lower
questions.explanation_en: Premiums must exceed expected payouts, so what you buy is never a return but the removal of the loss distribution's tail. Wealth grows multiplicatively, and a single wipeout takes you out of the game, so a negative-expectation premium that blocks ruin is rational. "I'm healthy, so I need less" is a named misconception: what you insure is precisely the unlikely case that doesn't look like you.

questions.question: 按「发生频率 × 后果严重度」的筛法，下列哪一项最应该投保？
options: 手机碎屏险，因为手机屏幕摔碎是最常见的意外
意外死亡与伤残险，作为已有定期寿险之外再加一层的额外保障
延长保修，因为家电坏了维修很麻烦
车险中的责任限额，防一场重伤事故带来的、没有上限的求偿
questions.explanation: 保险唯一的战场是低概率、后果毁灭的风险：车最多赔到车没了，重伤事故的求偿却没有天花板。碎屏、保修属于高频小额，买了等于付手续费；意外死亡险只赔特定死因，寿险已覆盖。
questions.question_en: Using the "frequency × severity" filter, which of these most deserves insurance?
options_en: Phone screen insurance, since a cracked screen is the most common mishap
Accidental death and dismemberment cover, as an extra layer on top of an existing term life policy
An extended warranty, since appliance repairs are a hassle
The liability limit on auto insurance, guarding against uncapped claims from a serious-injury accident
questions.explanation_en: Insurance's only battlefield is low-probability, catastrophic risk: the most a car can cost you is the car, but injury claims have no ceiling. Screens and warranties are frequent, small losses where you are just paying fees; AD&D pays only for specific causes of death that term life already covers.

questions.question: 关于免赔额，下列哪种做法最符合文中的原则？
options: 免赔额只是保险公司的定价技巧，跟个人的应急资金无关
设在能一次性拿出的现金范围内，并确认这笔钱真的备着
免赔额越高越好，因为这样保费最低，至于账上有没有对应的现金都无所谓
免赔额越低越安全，宁可多付保费也要把自付部分压到最小
questions.explanation: 免赔额是主动划下的自保线，接着应急基金来定：缓冲越厚，保险越便宜。最低免赔额多付的保费几年累计往往超过多扛的金额；真正危险的不是免赔额高，而是免赔额高、账上却没有那笔现金。
questions.question_en: Which approach to deductibles best fits the article's principles?
options_en: A deductible is just an insurer's pricing trick and has nothing to do with your emergency fund
Set it within the cash you could pay at once, and make sure that money really is set aside
The higher the deductible the better, since premiums are lowest; whether the cash is there doesn't matter
The lower the deductible the safer; pay more in premiums to minimize out-of-pocket costs
questions.explanation_en: A deductible is a self-insurance line you draw yourself, tied to your emergency fund: the thicker the buffer, the cheaper the insurance. The extra premium for a minimal deductible often exceeds, within a few years, the extra risk you would have carried; the real danger is not a high deductible but a high deductible with no cash to cover it.
